name: Horsehead Nebula
tagline: The dark horse of Orion — a cold dust silhouette against glowing hydrogen.
history: The Horsehead is the night sky's most recognizable silhouette — a pillar of cold, dense dust blocking the red glow of the emission nebula behind it. Sculpted by ultraviolet light from the bright star Sigma Orionis, the 'horse's head' is actually a star-forming pocket eroding at its edges. Herschel found it in 1781 but it went unremarked until photographic plates revealed its shape in 1888 — one of the first deep-sky objects ever imaged.
